issue.body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/kevva/next-server-action-network-error

### To Reproduce

1. Start the application (`npm run dev`)
2. Go to `/` and click "Submit", the server action should be called every 5s
3. Stop the server to simulate a network error

### Current vs. Expected behavior

So, I found this issue while building a magic link login in a React Native `WebView`. In my submit handler I'm polling for a login result by retrying calling a server action. However, when switching apps to open the magic link and then switching back, the app throws an exception. This is because in a `WebView` on iOS all requests seem to be cancelled when switching apps and Next.js doesn't seem to handle network errors in server actions very well.

The current behaviour don't let me catch the error at all, even though wrapping the server action in a `try/catch`. The expected behaviour would be to not throw before I can catch the error myself.

issue.title: ensure server action errors notify rejection handlers
issue.body:
### What
When attaching a rejection listener to a server action promise, in the case of network errors, the rejection handler would be skipped and it'd throw an error that crashes the application.

### Why
When we refactored these reducers to no longer suspend, it caused the rejection handling logic we have to no longer make sense. In this case we're working with a native promise that won't have a `status` property, so we'd re-throw the error and not call `reject`. 

### How
This removes the special status handling logic and makes the rejection handler always call `reject` with the error. This will either be handled by user code or let the error bubble to an error boundary. 

I also cleaned up some mutable code that is no longer needed now that these reducers aren't replayed. 

Closes NEXT-1715
Closes NEXT-2323
Fixes #58638
